text: A station can be accessible. Its network may not be. This is UNLOCK, the accessibility impact graph.
UNLOCK loads the open lift and platform data of all four hundred and one S.N.C.F. stations around Paris into one Relate graph file. This is Juvisy: twelve platforms, joined to an underpass by lifts.
Select lift A.S.C. three, between platforms fifty and fifty-one and the north underpass. Twenty-one confirmed step-free connections can use it.
Simulate an outage. The published data is not touched, but platforms fifty and fifty-one are cut off. Twenty-one connections move from confirmed, to blocked.

Why? Open a broken connection. This is the actual path in the graph: platform forty, lift A.S.C. eight, the underpass, lift A.S.C. three, platform fifty. Two lifts in series, each with its published status and source file.
Now rank every possible repair across the region. Fixing this lift restores twenty-one connections, ahead of two lifts that are really out of service today, at Mantes-la-Jolie and Noisy-le-Sec.
Apply the repair, and the network returns exactly to its published state. Every result is re-computed by an independent Cypher query, and the two agree.
Inside: one persistent Relate file, about six thousand nodes, the path query, and the statements it just ran.
UNLOCK doesn't just show you what's broken. It shows you what fixing it makes possible.
